blocks.task: use them to test yourself or a partner.

questions.q: Show that the area of an equilateral triangle of side 6 cm is 9√3 cm².
questions.model: Area = ½ × 6 × 6 × sin 60° = 18 × √3/2. = 9√3 cm²: every step written because the answer is given.

questions.q: Timed mixed section (portal, 20 minutes, 22 marks; command words highlighted). Sample: (a) show that the solutions of x² - 4x - 3 = 0 are 2 ± √7 [3] (b) the volume of a cone of radius 3 cm and height 8 cm, in terms of π [2] (c) a rectangle is 8.4 cm by 5.2 cm, each to 1 d.p.: the upper bound of its perimeter [2] (d) the exact value of (√12 + √3)² [3]
questions.model: (a) Complete the square: (x - 2)² - 4 - 3 = 0 (M1); (x - 2)² = 7 (M1); x = 2 ± √7 (A1). Every step shown, because the answer is given. (d) √12 = 2√3, so (3√3)² = 27.

questions.q: explain in the portal response box why 'x = 2.6' alone earns no marks when the question says 'show that the root is 2.6 to 1 d.p.'.
questions.a: The answer is given, so the marks are for the method and for a more accurate value (such as 2.63) that rounds to 2.6.

questions.q: Is the cosine rule on the 4MA1 Higher formulae sheet?
Which must you learn: the area of a circle or the volume of a sphere?
Big question: how can you gain marks on questions you cannot finish?
questions.a: Write a method for every part, use exact or unrounded values, follow the command words and return to unfinished parts at the end.
